topStories.headline: SFSU Enrollment Rises for First Time in More Than a Decade
topStories.dek: San Francisco State University enrolled 20,824 students for fall 2026, reversing years of decline with a 20 percent surge in new undergraduates.
topStories.body:
San Francisco State University is welcoming a larger student body this fall, marking the university's first enrollment increase in more than a decade — a significant turnaround following years of demographic and enrollment challenges. SFSU enrolled 20,824 students for fall 2026, with particularly strong growth among new students.

The university saw a 20 percent lift in new incoming freshman and transfer undergraduate enrollment. That is part of a year-over-year total new incoming student — first-year, first-year, transfer and graduate — increase of 18 percent.

The increase follows several years of focused work to strengthen recruitment, improve the experience of prospective and admitted students and position SFSU as a destination for students seeking an affordable, high-quality education in one of the world's most dynamic and innovative cities.

The numbers, published by SFSU on October 5, drew immediate attention across campus and in city media. The increased enrollment for fall 2026 at SFSU was discussed in multiple news segments on KGO-TV and KRON-TV.

"This growth did not happen overnight," President Lynn Mahoney said. "It reflects years of thoughtful planning and a tremendous amount of work across the University. We have been focused on what today's students need and expect from a university: a strong academic experience, a welcoming community and a clear path from college to a meaningful career. Students are responding, and that gives us tremendous momentum as we look to the future."

topStories.headline: Raising Cane's Fills Stonestown's Long-Empty McDonald's Slot — Opening Monday
topStories.dek: The Louisiana-based chicken chain opens its second San Francisco location at Stonestown Galleria on October 12, ending a two-year vacancy in the former McDonald's space.
topStories.body:
Raising Cane's will open its second San Francisco restaurant next week, less than a month after the fast-growing fried chicken chain made its city debut at Fisherman's Wharf. The Louisiana-based company said its newest location will open on Oct. 12 at Stonestown Galleria, taking over the former McDonald's space at 255 Winston Drive.

The restaurant replaces a McDonald's that operated at Stonestown for more than three decades before closing in 2024. The roughly 6,000-square-foot space remained vacant for about two years even as Stonestown continued to add new retailers and restaurants and emerged as one of San Francisco's busiest shopping centers.

The Louisiana-founded chain known for its chicken fingers, crinkle-cut fries and Texas toast plans to celebrate its grand opening with freebies for customers who line up early, including Cane's merch and free Cane's for a year for a lucky few. A ribbon-cutting ceremony will also include local high school and college cheerleaders.

The new restaurant's design includes artwork inspired by nearby schools, such as San Francisco State University. The mall eatery will be open late: until 2 a.m. from Sunday to Wednesday, and until 3:30 a.m. from Thursday to Saturday.

topStories.headline: SFSU's Historic Planetarium Hosts Final Free Shows Before Renovation Closes It
topStories.dek: The Charles F. Hagar Planetarium at SF State offers its last public shows through October 13 before shutting down for a long-planned modernization funded in part by a nearly $2 million grant.
topStories.body:
SFSU's Charles F. Hagar Planetarium in Thornton Hall will soon close temporarily for renovation. These are the last chances for the public to see its remarkable vintage star projector in action — and to witness the Milky Way as it appears far from city lights. Shows are free and open to the public.

Remaining shows include "A Few of My Favorite Things About the Hagar Planetarium" by Adrienne Cool on Friday, Oct. 9 at 5:30 p.m.; another session of the same show on Monday, Oct. 12 at 6:30 p.m.; and "Undead Stars and Spooky Constellation Stories" by Gillis Lowry on Tuesday, Oct. 13 at 1 p.m. Shows last about 45 minutes and last entry is five minutes after the start time.

The Charles F. Hagar Planetarium opened its doors in 1973. Since that time, it has served an estimated 100,000 visitors, including SF State students, San Francisco school children, community groups and members of the general public.

The university is embarking on a complete renovation of the planetarium beginning this summer. As part of the project, a new state-of-the-art star projector is coming from Zeiss in Germany. The renovation has received nearly $2 million from the Heising-Simons Foundation. The planetarium is located on the fourth floor of Thornton Hall, 1600 Holloway Avenue.

events.description: The SF State Observatory is a student-run facility open to members of the public on selected nights in fall semester. moreNews.headline: All SF Public Libraries Closed October 12 for Indigenous Peoples' Day
moreNews.body: All San Francisco Public Libraries, including the West Portal Branch at 190 Lenox Way, will be closed Monday, October 12 for Indigenous Peoples' Day. The branch reopens Tuesday, October 13.
